html:
Spiš Castle is a ruined castle on a limestone hill in eastern Slovakia, first built in the early 1100s. Its walls enclose about four hectares, making it one of the largest castle sites in Central Europe.

It guarded the Spiš region, a frontier of the Kingdom of Hungary settled by German colonists who built prosperous mining and trading towns such as Levoča. The castle held out against the Mongol invasion of 1241. Later it passed to the Zápolya and then the Thurzó and Csáky families. A fire in 1780 left it a ruin. It is now a World Heritage Site together with Levoča and the nearby church town of Spišská Kapitula.
sum: Spiš Castle is a ruined castle on a limestone hill in eastern Slovakia, first built in the early 1100s. Its walls enclose about four hectares, making it one of the largest castle sites in Central Europe.
